title: 1987 AHSME Problem 19
statement: Which of the following is closest to \(\sqrt{65}-\sqrt{63}?\)

solutions.text:
Rationalizing gives \[ \sqrt{65}-\sqrt{63}=\frac2{\sqrt{65}+\sqrt{63}}. \] The denominator is less than \(16,\) because its square is \(128+2\sqrt{4095}\lt256.\) Thus the value is greater than \(\frac{2}{16}=0.125.\) Also each radical exceeds \(7.5,\) so the value is less than \(\frac{2}{15}<0.134.\) It is therefore closer to \(0.13\) than to any other choice.

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Rationalize the difference of the two square roots
Compare \(\sqrt{65}+\sqrt{63}\) with \(16\) to decide which side of \(0.125\) the result lies on
